body:
Found while documenting #121 (per-profile spend), verified against src/stats.js on 2026-08-28.

## What

Since #119, every node a track runner claims in-session carries the runner's `session_id` and
`transcript_path` — the same file for the root and every node. `priceOf` (src/stats.js:207) reads
that transcript per attempt row, and `summarizeSpend` adds each row's usage, so one session's tokens
are counted once per node.

Reproduced with the module directly: three node attempts naming one transcript of 100 turns report
`spend.usage.turns = 300` and three times the estimate.

## Why it matters

A track is the recommended engine for coupled work, so the boards most likely to want a spend number
are exactly the ones that over-state it — silently, and by a factor nobody can see in the output.

## Direction

Sum usage per distinct transcript (or per `session_id`), not per attempt row: read each transcript
once, attribute it to one attempt, and leave the other rows of that session with no usage — or add a
`shared_with` count so the report can say "one session across N nodes". Either way `hkb stats`
should never print a total that double-counts a file it read twice.

Docs written in #121 describe the current behaviour as a caveat; update them with the fix.

Scope: src/stats.js, test/stats.test.js, and the track paragraph in docs/harnesses.md.
goal: a track session is counted once, however many nodes carry its transcript
title: hkb stats counts a track's one transcript once per node
